itemOffered.name: Inquest Representation
itemOffered.description: An inquest is an inquiry in the Coroner's Court into how someone died. It is not a trial and decides no one's guilt. Astons Law Chambers represents families and interested persons at the pre-inquest review and at the inquest itself.

itemOffered.name: Pre-Inquest Review Hearings and Scope Arguments
itemOffered.description: Representation at the pre-inquest review, which fixes the scope, witnesses, and timetable for the substantive inquest.

itemOffered.name: Article 2 Inquest Representation
itemOffered.description: Specialist representation for inquests requiring Article 2 compliance, ensuring thorough investigation into deaths involving public bodies.

itemOffered.name: Witness Examination at Substantive Inquest
itemOffered.description: Examination of witnesses at the substantive inquest hearing.

itemOffered.name: Disclosure Review and Documentary Preparation
itemOffered.description: Review of disclosure and preparation of documentary evidence and witness questions.

mainEntity.name: Can a family instruct directly for inquest representation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Inquest instructions are accepted under the Direct Access scheme where suitable. The first call covers whether the case is appropriate for direct instruction.

A pre-inquest review is the procedural hearing that fixes the scope, witnesses, and timetable for the substantive inquest. Your position before the pre-inquest review matters — it is where the scope of the inquiry is decided.

mainEntity.name: Is legal aid available for inquest representation?

acceptedAnswer.text: In some cases, yes — typically through a solicitor with a legal aid contract. Astons Law Chambers can refer where this is the right route.
